title: Key derivation functions (PBKDF2, scrypt, Argon2, HKDF)
summary: Key derivation functions (KDFs) derive cryptographic keys from a password or shared secret. PBKDF2: applies a pseudorandom function (HMAC) repeatedly (iterations) with a salt. scrypt: memory-hard (uses large memory to resist GPU/ASIC attacks). Argon2: winner of the Password Hashing Competition (2015), memory-hard, with variants (Argon2d, Argon2i, Argon2id). HKDF: extract-then-expand for deriving keys from a shared secret (not password-based).
aliases: Key derivation functions (PBKDF2, scrypt, Argon2, HKDF)

ext.summary: Key derivation functions (KDFs) derive cryptographic keys from a password or shared secret. PBKDF2: applies a pseudorandom function (HMAC) repeatedly (iterations) with a salt. scrypt: memory-hard (uses large memory to resist GPU/ASIC attacks). Argon2: winner of the Password Hashing Competition (2015), memory-hard, with variants (Argon2d, Argon2i, Argon2id). HKDF: extract-then-expand for deriving keys from a shared secret (not password-based).

structure.meaning: DK = T_1 || T_2 || ... || T_dklen/hlen, where T_i = F(password, salt, c, i) and F = U_1 XOR U_2 XOR ... XOR U_c, U_1 = PRF(password, salt || INT(i)), U_j = PRF(password, U_{j-1}).
PRF (HMAC-SHA256), salt (>= 128 bits), iterations (>= 100000 for passwords), key length.
Memory-hard: uses ROMix (random memory access) and BlockMix. Params: N (CPU/memory cost, power of 2), r (block size), p (parallelism).

Memory-hard with time cost (t), memory cost (m), parallelism (p). Variants: Argon2d (data-dependent, faster, GPU-resistant), Argon2i (data-independent, side-channel resistant), Argon2id (hybrid, recommended).
Extract: PRK = HMAC-Hash(salt, IKM). Expand: OKM = T_1 || T_2 || ... where T_i = HMAC-Hash(PRK, T_{i-1} || info || i).
Hash (SHA-256), salt (optional), IKM (input key material), info (context), output length.

notes: PBKDF2 is the oldest (RFC 2898, 2000) but not memory-hard (vulnerable to GPU/ASIC).
scrypt (RFC 7914) is memory-hard but complex to tune.
Argon2 (RFC 9106) is the recommended password hashing function (PHC winner).
HKDF is for deriving keys from a shared secret (not passwords). Used in TLS 1.3, Signal Protocol.
Password hashing should use Argon2id with appropriate parameters (m=64MB, t=3, p=4).
